review_notes: I read the whole file and its uses in Equivalence.lean, Graded.lean, UniversalProperty.lean and Descent/AffineMorphism.lean. I also looked at the related relativeSpecCover_f_relativeSpecToBase lemma in Basic.lean. I could not run Lean, so I did not test any claim about simp behaviour. Both findings are about simp design. The first, about non-confluence, is a credible risk but speculative. The second, about the missing inverse-side lemma, is a smaller interface gap. I found no problems with the other simp lemmas: the Iso hom and inv lemmas, the naturality lemma and the counit .left lemmas all have sensible orientation and head symbols.

findings.problem: Two simp lemmas can fire on the same composite and give different results. The cover-chart lemma and its `_assoc` form rewrite `relativeSpecCover.f U ≫ relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme` into the explicit `Spec.map … ≫ fromSpec`. The `_comp` lemma rewrites `relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme ≫ p` into `relativeSpecToBase`. Take `cover.f U ≫ rSFTS ≫ p`. Simp reduces the inner `rSFTS ≫ p` first and gets `cover.f U ≫ relativeSpecToBase`. Take `(cover.f U ≫ rSFTS) ≫ p`. Simp reduces the inner `cover.f U ≫ rSFTS` first and gets `Spec.map … ≫ fromSpec ≫ p`. The two results may differ, and neither is reduced to the other. The sibling lemma `relativeSpecCover_f_relativeSpecToBase` is deliberately not simp, so the explicit-chart form is not a canonical normal form elsewhere. The cover-chart lemma also expands an abstract cover map into explicit Spec/fromSpec terms. In this library it is only ever applied by explicit term or `rw` (Equivalence.lean:85, Counit.lean:136, 224–225), never by `simp`. I did not run Lean, so the non-confluence is a risk and not an observed failure.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `simp` from `relativeSpecCover_f_relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme` and keep only `@[reassoc]`. Callers that need the chart form can use `rw` or the term, as they already do. Alternatively, keep `simp` and also add `@[simp]` to `relativeSpecCover_f_relativeSpecToBase`, so that both composites reduce to the same chart form.
findings.benefit: Simp calls on goals mentioning `relativeSpecCover.f U` no longer give different, non-confluent normal forms depending on how the composition is parenthesised. Goals are not silently expanded into `Spec.map … ≫ fromSpec`. No existing proof in the repo depends on the simp use.

findings.problem: The simp set normalises the inverse recovery map to `inv p.relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme`. The forward map has a simp lemma `relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme_comp`, which says `rSFTS ≫ p = relativeSpecToBase`. The inverse has no matching simp lemma for its structure map. There is no lemma for `inv p.relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme ≫ p.pushforwardStructureAlgebra.relativeSpecToBase = p`, and none for the form with `p` on the other side. Downstream, `toDescended` (Descent/AffineMorphism.lean:117–119) is defined with `inv (X.hom ≫ p).relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme`. Its structure-map lemma `toDescended_hom` is proved by rewriting with `cancel_epi` and then `relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme_comp`. A simp lemma would not close it, because the `inv` form has no simp rule for how it composes with the structure morphism.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma such as `@[reassoc (attr := simp)] lemma inv_relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme_comp : inv p.relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme ≫ p.pushforwardStructureAlgebra.relativeSpecToBase = p`. Prove it with `IsIso.inv_comp_eq` and the existing `relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme_comp`, or by `rw [IsIso.inv_comp_eq, relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme_comp]`. Also consider a simp lemma `inv p.relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme ≫ g = …` that matches the existing naturality lemma. `inv_relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme_naturality` is currently reassoc only, but it already has the shape `g ≫ inv q.rSFTS = inv p.rSFTS ≫ relativeSpecMap …`, so it is a natural simp candidate too.
findings.benefit: The inverse normal form chosen by `relativeSpecFunctionsIso_inv` and `relativeSpecCounit_inv_app_left` would get the same simp coverage as the forward map. Over-base proofs involving the inverse counit, such as `toDescended_hom`, could be closed by `simp` and would no longer need the `cancel_epi` rewrite.
